statements.venue: Letter to President Trump from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen
statements.quote: a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, the development of biological weapons, and other dangerous activities that threaten the lives of the American people and humanity writ large.
statements.context: The letter urged the President to negotiate an agreement on AI guardrails with China's President Xi at their planned 24 September 2026 summit.
statements.reason: The letter she signed says frontier AI development could enable biological weapons and other activities that threaten humanity as a whole, which is level A under the threat-to-humanity ruling; these are the letter's words, not her own, and a reviewer could read it as B (mass-casualty misuse).

statements.venue: Letter to President Trump from 17 Senate Democrats, led by Sen. Van Hollen
statements.quote: AI technology is too powerful, and its risks too many, for the U.S. and China to forgo discussions on parameters around its development and use.
statements.context: The closing passage of the same letter, arguing that the United States and China must talk directly about limits on AI development and use.
statements.reason: This passage of the letter she signed acknowledges serious risks from AI in general terms without naming a catastrophic harm.

slowdown.note: She signed the 23 September 2026 letter calling for a formal agreement with China that would slow down frontier AI development to prevent cyberattacks, bioweapons and other threats; this is a signed letter, not her own statement.

pause.note: The letter she signed asks for an agreement that would 'potentially enact a mutual pause' in frontier AI development, so the pause is tentative and conditional on China joining.

intl.note: She signed the 23 September 2026 letter urging direct talks and a formal agreement with China to slow, and possibly mutually pause, frontier AI development.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Signed the letter from 17 Senate Democrats urging President Trump to negotiate an AI agreement with China, including a slowdown and possible mutual pause in frontier AI development.

grade_reason: The only evidence is the 23 September 2026 letter she co-signed, which says frontier AI development could enable activities that threaten humanity writ large. No statement in her own words about catastrophic AI risk was found.
notes: All 6 required web searches have now run, over two runs. In the first run 5 ran and the 6th (her name with "AI safety") was refused with a too-many-requests error; it was run successfully in a second run on 11 November 2026 and returned nothing about her: every result was about Microsoft president Brad Smith or AI safety in general, plus one Senate hearing record from the 118th Congress (2023-2024), which is before the date range and was not opened. No lead appeared, so no follow-up search was run and nothing was added. In the first run I also opened her official site's own search page for 'artificial intelligence', which showed one relevant 2025-2026 item (the 2 October 2026 data center tax letter, level D, listed in record only). Both quotes were checked character for character against the Van Hollen press release page, which I downloaded directly; curly apostrophes on that page do not occur inside the quotes. The first quote starts mid-sentence (the sentence begins 'America leads in AI innovation, and we must lead the world in AI safety and international cooperation, including by working with China to develop'). The A level rests on the phrase 'humanity writ large' in a co-signed letter and is flagged boundary. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (September 2026): no source found showing she co-sponsored it; the coverage seen named only Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar, and I did not check the bill's co-sponsor list on congress.gov. No press release on her own site about the China letter was found. Her other AI-related items on smith.senate.gov (AI in eviction filings, 2024; algorithmic rent pricing; DOGE use of AI on student loan data) are outside the date range or outside catastrophic risk.
